# Model and source

* Citation: Yu R, Toutain P-L, Ekstrand C, Jusko WJ. Meta-Analysis and
  Physiologically-Based Modeling of the Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics
  of Dexamethasone in Horses. Pharm Res. 2026.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-026-04120-5>
* Open-access full text: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13593757/>

Yu 2026 pooled the mean dexamethasone (DEX) concentration-time data of 12
published horse studies -- intravenous (IV), intramuscular (IM), oral and
intra-articular (IA) dosing of DEX alcohol, DEX sodium phosphate (PHO) and DEX
isonicotinate (ISO) -- and fitted them with ADAPT 5 to a minimal
physiologically based PK (mPBPK) model linked to two indirect-response PD
models: inhibition of a circadian cortisol production rate (adrenal
suppression) and stimulation of glucose production.

The packaged model reproduces the ADAPT code in the paper's Supplementary
Materials:

* **Disposition.** Blood (`a_blood`), liver (`a_liver`) and a lumped
  remainder tissue (`a_remainder`) with physiological volumes and blood flows
  of a typical 550-kg horse. DEX binds saturably in the liver (capacity
  `Bmax`, affinity `Kd`); hepatic metabolism acts on unbound liver DEX and
  renal clearance on plasma DEX.
* **Inputs.** Each route and form has its own dosing compartment:

| Dose | `cmt` | Amount to give |
|------|-------|----------------|
| IV DEX alcohol | `a_blood` | ug DEX |
| IV DEX sodium phosphate | `blood_pho` | ug of the prodrug |
| IV DEX isonicotinate | `blood_iso` | ug of the prodrug |
| IM DEX alcohol | `depot_im` | ug DEX |
| IM DEX sodium phosphate | `depot_im_pho` | ug of the prodrug |
| IM DEX isonicotinate | `depot_im_iso` | ug of the prodrug |
| Oral powder or tablet | `depot_oral_solid` | ug DEX |
| Oral suspension or solution | `depot_oral_liquid` | ug DEX |
| IA DEX sodium phosphate, healthy joint | `joint_pho` | ug of the prodrug |
| IA DEX sodium phosphate, inflamed joint | `joint_inflamed1`, `joint_inflamed2`, `joint_inflamed3` (the same amount into all three, at the same time) | ug of the prodrug |

  The prodrug-to-DEX mass conversion (molecular weights 516.41, 492.54 and
  392.46) is applied inside the model.
* **Clock time.** Model time is the clock time in hours after midnight of the
  first study day: a dose at 8 AM is given at `time = 8`. The cortisol
  baseline is a 24-h cosine whose acrophase is a clock time, so this is what
  places the dose on the circadian cycle.
* **Outputs.** `Cc` (plasma DEX, ng/mL), `Curine` (urine DEX, ng/mL),
  `Csynovial` (synovial-fluid DEX, ng/mL), `cortisol` (ng/mL) and `glucose`
  (mmol/L).

The cortisol and glucose baselines (`lrbase_cortisol`, `lamp_cortisol`,
`lrbase_glucose`) and the size of the post-dose stress surge (`lrmax_stress`)
were estimated study by study. The packaged defaults are the values the paper
itself used to predict a new study (Fig. 8: the Ekstrand 2019 baseline and the
mean surge of 50.53 ng/mL); the figure replications below override them with
each study's values.

```{r load-model}
mod_fn <- readModelDb("Yu_2026_dexamethasone_horse_mpbpk")
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_fn)

# Prodrug mass per unit DEX-equivalent mass (Yu 2026 Methods)
dex_to_pho <- 516.41 / 392.46
dex_to_iso <- 492.54 / 392.46
```

```{r helpers}
# One subject's event table. `doses` has columns time, cmt, amt and optionally
# rate. Observation rows are put on the `glucose` state, which is itself a
# declared endpoint, so every output column (Cc, Curine, Csynovial, cortisol,
# glucose) comes back on every observation row.
build_events <- function(id, doses, obs_times) {
  if (is.null(doses$rate)) {
    doses$rate <- 0
  }
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    id = id,
    time = doses$time,
    evid = 1L,
    cmt = doses$cmt,
    amt = doses$amt,
    rate = doses$rate
  )
  obs_rows <- data.frame(
    id = id,
    time = obs_times,
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = "glucose",
    amt = 0,
    rate = 0
  )
  dplyr::arrange(rbind(dose_rows, obs_rows), time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

simulate_one <- function(doses, obs_times, params = NULL, label = NA_character_) {
  ev <- build_events(1L, doses, obs_times)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, params = params, returnType = "data.frame")
  out$label <- label
  out
}

# Dose rows for the inflamed-joint route: the same prodrug amount into the
# three synovial-fluid pools at the same time.
inflamed_ia <- function(time, prodrug_ug) {
  data.frame(
    time = time,
    cmt = c("joint_inflamed1", "joint_inflamed2", "joint_inflamed3"),
    amt = prodrug_ug
  )
}

pk_grid <- function(start, end) {
  sort(unique(c(
    start + c(0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.17, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
    seq(start + 1, end, by = 0.5)
  )))
}
```

# Population

The 12 studies (Yu 2026 Table I) used Saddlebred, Standardbred, Thoroughbred,
Quarter Horse and warmblood horses aged 2-22 years and weighing 385-700 kg:
females, stallions and geldings, at least 6 horses per study except the
lipopolysaccharide (LPS) synovitis study, which gave each IA dose to one horse.
All horses were healthy apart from that synovitis study. The data are study
means, digitised from the publications or taken from the authors' original
measurements, so the model describes the typical horse and carries no
between-animal variability. Physiological volumes and flows are those of a
typical 550-kg horse (Table S1). The same information is available via
`readModelDb("Yu_2026_dexamethasone_horse_mpbpk")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. In summary:

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Prodrug kinetics in blood, IM depots, oral depot | -- | Eqs. 1-4; ADAPT PK code |
| Healthy-joint prodrug conversion and DEX absorption | -- | Eqs. 5-6; ADAPT code (Dose 21) |
| Inflamed-joint synovial-fluid DEX (tri-exponential) | -- | Eq. 7 |
| Blood, liver, remainder mass balance | -- | Eqs. 8-10 as coded in ADAPT (`XP(2)`-`XP(4)`) |
| Liver unbound fraction (saturable binding) | -- | Eq. 11; ADAPT `Kp1` |
| Urine concentration | -- | Eq. 12 |
| Cortisol baseline, production rate, IDR I with stress surge | -- | Eqs. 13-16; ADAPT cortisol code |
| Glucose IDR III | -- | Eq. 17; ADAPT glucose code |
| `lvblood`, `lvliver`, `lvremainder`, `lqliver`, `lqremainder` | 38.896 L, 7.15 L, 503.954 L, 651.55 L/h, 1311.99 L/h | ADAPT code; Table S1 (rounded) |
| `bpr` | 0.6945 | ADAPT code (Methods: 0.69) |
| `lqurine` | 0.494 L/h | Methods (Eq. 12) |
| `lbmax_liver`, `lkd_liver` | 140.1, 0.269 ng/mL | Table II |
| `lkp_remainder` | 1.09 | Table II |
| `lclint`, `lclr` | 473.6, 5.69 mL/h/kg | Table II |
| `lkf_pho`, `lkf_iso` | 16.67, 20.59 1/h | Table II |
| `lfconv_pho`, `lfconv_iso` | 1 (fixed), 0.695 | Table II |
| `lka_im`, `lka_im_pho`, `lka_im_iso` | 0.131, 2.95, 0.0105 1/h | Table II |
| `lfdepot_im` | 1 (fixed) | ADAPT cortisol and glucose code (`Fml = 1`) |
| `lka_oral_solid`, `lka_oral_liquid` | 0.421, 0.529 1/h | Table II |
| `lfgi_solid`, `lfgi_liquid` | 0.521, 0.682 | Table II |
| `lkf_ia_pho` | 30 1/h (fixed) | Table II |
| `lka_ia`, `lfia` | 2.61 1/h, 0.830 | Table II (healthy joints) |
| `lka_ia_inflamed`, `lfia_inflamed` | 5.13 1/h, 1 (fixed) | Table II (inflamed joints) |
| `ffrac_sf1`-`ffrac_sf3`, `lalpha_sf`, `lbeta_sf`, `lgamma_sf` | 0.9783, 0.02098, 0.0007512; 6.354, 0.5977, 0.07056 1/h | Results, IA paragraph |
| `lvsf` | 16.9 mL | Methods |
| `lrbase_cortisol`, `lamp_cortisol` | 62.25, 22.01 ng/mL | Table III (Ekstrand 2019, as used for Fig. 8) |
| `tacro_cortisol` | 8.94 h (8:56 AM) | ADAPT cortisol code; Table III |
| `lkout_cortisol` | 0.405 1/h | Table III |
| `lic50_cortisol`, `imax_cortisol` | 0.0383 ng/mL, 1 (fixed) | Table III |
| `lrmax_stress`, `ltau_stress` | 50.53 ng/mL, 0.34 h (fixed) | Results (Fig. 8 paragraph); Table III |
| `lrbase_glucose` | 5.14 mmol/L | Results: maximal glucose 11.24 mM = E0 (1 + 1.187) |
| `lkout_glucose` | 0.0485 1/h | Table III |
| `lemax_glucose`, `lec50_glucose` | 0.799, 1.187 ng/mL | Table III values as assigned by the ADAPT glucose code (Table III prints them the other way round; see Figure 9 below) |
| Residual errors | 0 (not reported) | Eq. 18 gives the form only |

# Pharmacokinetics

## Figure 2: intravenous dosing

```{r fig2}
# Replicates Figure 2 of Yu 2026. Doses are DEX-equivalent mg/kg times the
# study mean body weight recorded in the ADAPT code comments; prodrug doses
# are converted to prodrug mass. All doses at time 0.
iv_studies <- list(
  list(label = "1984 DEX 0.05 mg/kg", cmt = "a_blood", mgkg = 0.05, bw = 556.67, conv = 1),
  list(label = "1984 ISO 0.05 mg/kg", cmt = "blood_iso", mgkg = 0.05, bw = 556.67, conv = dex_to_iso),
  list(label = "2020 PHO 0.056 mg/kg", cmt = "blood_pho", mgkg = 0.056, bw = 534, conv = dex_to_pho),
  list(label = "1996 DEX 0.0225 mg/kg", cmt = "a_blood", mgkg = 0.0225, bw = 443.7, conv = 1),
  list(label = "2010 DEX 0.008 mg/kg", cmt = "a_blood", mgkg = 0.008, bw = 522.63, conv = 1),
  list(label = "2013 PHO 0.05 mg/kg", cmt = "blood_pho", mgkg = 0.05, bw = 523.5, conv = dex_to_pho),
  list(label = "2005 DEX 0.05 mg/kg", cmt = "a_blood", mgkg = 0.05, bw = 514.5, conv = 1),
  list(label = "2018 PHO 0.0073 mg/kg", cmt = "blood_pho", mgkg = 0.0073, bw = 521, conv = dex_to_pho)
)
fig2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(iv_studies, function(s) {
  simulate_one(
    data.frame(time = 0, cmt = s$cmt, amt = s$mgkg * 1000 * s$bw * s$conv),
    pk_grid(0, 100),
    label = s$label
  )
}))

# Ekstrand 2016: DEX_PHO bolus plus a 3-h infusion (DEX-equivalent ug/kg),
# 507.92 kg.
infusion_levels <- c(0.1, 1, 10)
fig2_inf <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(infusion_levels, function(b) {
  bw <- 507.92
  doses <- data.frame(
    time = c(0, 0),
    cmt = "blood_pho",
    amt = c(b, 0.233 * b * 3) * bw * dex_to_pho,
    rate = c(0, 0.233 * b * bw * dex_to_pho)
  )
  simulate_one(doses, pk_grid(0, 100), label = sprintf("2016 PHO %g ug/kg + %g ug/kg/h x 3 h", b, 0.233 * b))
}))

dplyr::bind_rows(fig2, fig2_inf) |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1e-4, 1e4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Plasma DEX (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Yu 2026 (typical-value predictions)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

## Figure 3: intramuscular dosing, plasma and urine

```{r fig3}
# Replicates Figure 3 of Yu 2026: IM DEX alcohol 0.05 mg/kg (1984, 556.67 kg),
# IM DEX_PHO 0.05 mg/kg (2013, 523.5 kg) and IM DEX_ISO 0.024 mg/kg DEX
# equivalent (2015, 474.17 kg; urine shown dashed).
im_studies <- list(
  list(label = "1984 DEX 0.05 mg/kg", cmt = "depot_im", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 556.67),
  list(label = "2013 PHO 0.05 mg/kg", cmt = "depot_im_pho", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 523.5 * dex_to_pho),
  list(label = "2015 ISO 0.024 mg/kg", cmt = "depot_im_iso", amt = 0.0239 * 1000 * 474.17 * dex_to_iso)
)
fig3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(im_studies, function(s) {
  simulate_one(data.frame(time = 0, cmt = s$cmt, amt = s$amt), pk_grid(0, 360), label = s$label)
}))

fig3_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(fig3, matrix = "plasma", conc = Cc),
  dplyr::filter(fig3, label == "2015 ISO 0.024 mg/kg") |>
    dplyr::mutate(matrix = "urine", conc = Curine)
)
fig3_long |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = label, linetype = matrix)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1e-3, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Plasma or urine DEX (ng/mL)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Yu 2026 (typical-value predictions)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Figure 5: intra-articular dosing

```{r fig5}
# Replicates Figure 5 of Yu 2026: IA DEX_PHO 26.17 mg DEX equivalent into a
# healthy joint (Soma 2013) and 0.01-3 mg DEX equivalent into joints with
# LPS-induced synovitis (Ekstrand 2019).
ia_healthy <- simulate_one(
  data.frame(time = 0, cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 26170 * dex_to_pho),
  pk_grid(0, 36),
  label = "2013 healthy 26.17 mg"
)
ia_doses_mg <- c(3, 1, 0.3, 0.1, 0.03, 0.01)
ia_inflamed <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(ia_doses_mg, function(d) {
  simulate_one(inflamed_ia(0, d * 1000 * dex_to_pho), pk_grid(0, 36), label = sprintf("2019 synovitis %g mg", d))
}))
fig5 <- dplyr::bind_rows(ia_healthy, ia_inflamed)

fig5_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(ia_inflamed, matrix = "Synovial fluid", conc = Csynovial),
  dplyr::mutate(fig5, matrix = "Plasma", conc = Cc)
)
fig5_long |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, conc > 1e-3) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~matrix, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "DEX (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Yu 2026 (typical-value predictions)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The synovial-fluid curve starts at the whole DEX-equivalent dose in 16.9 mL,
e.g. 3 mg / 16.9 mL = 1.8e5 ng/mL, which is the top of the published Figure 5
left panel.

```{r fig5-check}
sf_3mg <- dplyr::filter(ia_inflamed, label == "2019 synovitis 3 mg")
sf0 <- sf_3mg$Csynovial[sf_3mg$time == 0]
# Deterministic: the t = 0 value is dose / VSF exactly (the three Eq. 7
# intercepts sum to 1.00003).
stopifnot(abs(sf0 / (3000 / 0.0169) - 1) < 1e-3)
```

## Published secondary quantities

The paper quotes a number of quantities derived from the fitted model. Each is
recomputed here from a fresh simulation of the packaged model.

```{r secondary}
bw <- 550
dose_ref <- 0.05 * 1000 * bw # 0.05 mg/kg DEX, typical 550-kg horse
grid_long <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.001), seq(1, 480, by = 0.05))))

iv_ref <- simulate_one(data.frame(time = 0, cmt = "a_blood", amt = dose_ref), grid_long)
# Log-trapezoid on the falling limb: the IV bolus decays at about 70 1/h for
# the first few minutes, which a linear trapezoid overstates.
auc_log_down <- function(time, conc) {
  dt <- diff(time)
  c1 <- head(conc, -1)
  c2 <- tail(conc, -1)
  use_log <- c2 < c1 & c2 > 0
  seg <- ifelse(use_log, (c1 - c2) / log(c1 / c2) * dt, (c1 + c2) / 2 * dt)
  sum(seg)
}
auc_iv <- auc_log_down(iv_ref$time, iv_ref$Cc)
cl_iv <- dose_ref / auc_iv / bw * 1000 # mL/h/kg

half_life <- function(s, t1, t2) {
  c1 <- s$Cc[which.min(abs(s$time - t1))]
  c2 <- s$Cc[which.min(abs(s$time - t2))]
  log(2) * (t2 - t1) / log(c1 / c2)
}
t_5pg <- min(iv_ref$time[iv_ref$time > 1 & iv_ref$Cc < 0.005])

po_solid <- simulate_one(data.frame(time = 0, cmt = "depot_oral_solid", amt = dose_ref), grid_long)
po_liquid <- simulate_one(data.frame(time = 0, cmt = "depot_oral_liquid", amt = dose_ref), grid_long)
f_solid <- auc_log_down(po_solid$time, po_solid$Cc) / auc_iv
f_liquid <- auc_log_down(po_liquid$time, po_liquid$Cc) / auc_iv

# Urinary DEX vs the 0.2 ng/mL harmonised screening limit
im_iso_urine <- simulate_one(
  data.frame(time = 0, cmt = "depot_im_iso", amt = 0.03 * 1000 * bw),
  seq(0, 480, by = 0.5)
)
t_hsl_im_iso <- min(im_iso_urine$time[im_iso_urine$time > 50 & im_iso_urine$Curine < 0.2]) / 24
iv_pho_urine <- simulate_one(
  data.frame(time = 0, cmt = "blood_pho", amt = 0.06 * 1000 * bw),
  seq(0, 120, by = 0.05)
)
t_hsl_iv_pho <- min(iv_pho_urine$time[iv_pho_urine$time > 1 & iv_pho_urine$Curine < 0.2])

c_iso_15d <- fig3$Cc[fig3$label == "2015 ISO 0.024 mg/kg" & fig3$time == 360]

secondary <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Total CL after 0.05 mg/kg IV (mL/h/kg)",
    "Half-life, 5-15 h phase (h)",
    "Half-life, 2-4 day phase (h)",
    "Time to 5 pg/mL after 0.05 mg/kg IV (h)",
    "Oral F, powder / tablet (%)",
    "Oral F, suspension / solution (%)",
    "Urine-to-plasma ratio",
    "Urine < 0.2 ng/mL after 0.03 mg/kg IM DEX_ISO (days)",
    "Urine < 0.2 ng/mL after 0.06 mg/kg IV DEX_PHO (h)",
    "Plasma DEX on day 15 after IM DEX_ISO 0.024 mg/kg (pg/mL)"
  ),
  Published = c(344, 2.6, 11, 67, 37.2, 48.7, 6.3, 11.5, 40, 10),
  Simulated = c(
    cl_iv,
    half_life(iv_ref, 5, 15),
    half_life(iv_ref, 48, 96),
    t_5pg,
    100 * f_solid,
    100 * f_liquid,
    iv_ref$Curine[200] / iv_ref$Cc[200],
    t_hsl_im_iso,
    t_hsl_iv_pho,
    1000 * c_iso_15d
  )
)
secondary$`% diff` <- 100 * (secondary$Simulated / secondary$Published - 1)
knitr::kable(secondary, digits = c(0, 2, 2, 1))
```

```{r secondary-check}
# Deterministic typical-value model, so these are numerical-integration and
# rounding tolerances, not sampling tolerances.
stopifnot(
  # CL = CLh + CLr from the well-stirred liver (338 + 5.69 mL/h/kg)
  abs(secondary$`% diff`[1]) < 2,
  # Phase half-lives quoted to two significant figures
  abs(secondary$`% diff`[2]) < 5,
  abs(secondary$`% diff`[3]) < 5,
  # Within 5%: see Assumptions and deviations
  abs(secondary$`% diff`[4]) < 6,
  abs(secondary$`% diff`[5]) < 3,
  abs(secondary$`% diff`[6]) < 3,
  # CLr / Vu = 3.13 / 0.494 exactly
  abs(secondary$`% diff`[7]) < 1.5,
  abs(secondary$`% diff`[8]) < 3,
  # "within 40 h": the urine curve crosses 0.2 ng/mL just after 40 h
  secondary$Simulated[9] < 45,
  # "remained twofold above a 5 pg/mL threshold"
  secondary$Simulated[10] > 10
)
```

The 5 pg/mL crossing (`r round(t_5pg, 1)` h against the published 67 h) and
the HSL crossing after the IV DEX_PHO dose (`r round(t_hsl_iv_pho, 1)` h against
"within 40 h") are within a few hours of the paper; both sit on the 11-h
terminal phase, so a few percent of the threshold-crossing time corresponds to
a few percent in concentration.

# PKNCA validation

Single doses to a 550-kg horse by every route (0.05 mg/kg DEX equivalent;
0.024 mg/kg for IM DEX_ISO as in Figure 3), compared against the peak times
and clearance the paper reports.

```{r pknca}
routes <- data.frame(
  treatment = c(
    "IV DEX", "IM DEX", "IM DEX_PHO", "IM DEX_ISO", "Oral powder/tablet", "Oral suspension/solution"
  ),
  cmt = c("a_blood", "depot_im", "depot_im_pho", "depot_im_iso", "depot_oral_solid", "depot_oral_liquid"),
  conv = c(1, 1, dex_to_pho, dex_to_iso, 1, 1),
  # DEX-equivalent mg/kg; DEX_ISO at the 0.024 mg/kg dose of Figure 3, whose
  # 21-h peak the paper quotes
  mgkg = c(0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.024, 0.05, 0.05),
  route = c("intravascular", rep("extravascular", 5))
)
grid_nca <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.01), seq(2, 480, by = 0.25))))
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(routes)), function(i) {
  out <- simulate_one(
    data.frame(time = 0, cmt = routes$cmt[i], amt = routes$mgkg[i] * 1000 * bw * routes$conv[i]),
    grid_nca
  )
  out$id <- i
  out$treatment <- routes$treatment[i]
  out
}))

conc_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(nrow(routes)),
  time = 0,
  amt = routes$mgkg * 1000 * bw,
  treatment = routes$treatment,
  route = routes$route
)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "route")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE,
  cl.obs = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)

# PKNCA returns CL in L/h for the 550-kg horse; the paper reports mL/h/kg.
nca_tbl$PPORRES[nca_tbl$PPTESTCD == "cl.obs"] <-
  nca_tbl$PPORRES[nca_tbl$PPTESTCD == "cl.obs"] * 1000 / bw
# CL only for the IV arm (the extravascular arms would give CL/F); tmax only
# for the extravascular arms.
nca_tbl <- nca_tbl[
  !(nca_tbl$PPTESTCD == "cl.obs" & nca_tbl$treatment != "IV DEX") &
    !(nca_tbl$PPTESTCD == "tmax" & nca_tbl$treatment == "IV DEX"),
]

reference <- data.frame(
  treatment = c(
    "IV DEX", "IM DEX", "IM DEX_PHO", "IM DEX_ISO", "Oral powder/tablet", "Oral suspension/solution"
  ),
  tmax = c(NA, 4.7, 0.23, 21, 2.7, 2.2),
  cl.obs = c(344, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA)
)
cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_tbl[nca_tbl$PPTESTCD %in% c("tmax", "cl.obs"), ],
  reference,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(tmax = "h", cl.obs = "mL/h/kg")
)
knitr::kable(cmp)
```

The published IM and oral peak times are those of the fitted curves in
Figures 3 and 4 at the studies' own doses ("0.23, 4.7, and 21 h in Fig. 3"; oral
"2.2 and 2.7 h", assigned here to the faster liquid and slower solid
absorption). Because liver binding is saturable, the peak time of the slow
DEX_ISO depot depends on dose (about 17 h at 0.05 mg/kg against about 22 h at
the 0.024 mg/kg dose of Figure 3).

```{r pknca-check}
cl_nca <- nca_tbl$PPORRES[nca_tbl$PPTESTCD == "cl.obs"]
tmax_nca <- setNames(
  nca_tbl$PPORRES[nca_tbl$PPTESTCD == "tmax"],
  nca_tbl$treatment[nca_tbl$PPTESTCD == "tmax"]
)
stopifnot(
  abs(cl_nca / 344 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(tmax_nca[["IM DEX"]] - 4.7) < 0.5,
  abs(tmax_nca[["IM DEX_PHO"]] - 0.23) < 0.05,
  abs(tmax_nca[["IM DEX_ISO"]] - 21) < 3,
  abs(tmax_nca[["Oral powder/tablet"]] - 2.7) < 0.5,
  abs(tmax_nca[["Oral suspension/solution"]] - 2.2) < 0.5
)
```

# Pharmacodynamics

## Figure 7: cortisol

The per-study baseline and stress-surge values below are those in the
authors' ADAPT cortisol code, which match the baselines drawn in Figure 7 (see
Assumptions and deviations for how they relate to the Table III footnotes).

```{r fig7}
# Replicates Figure 7 of Yu 2026. clock = clock time of the dose (h after
# midnight); rm / ra / rmax = study baseline mesor, amplitude and stress surge
# (ng/mL); doses as DEX-equivalent mg/kg at the study body weight.
cort_studies <- list(
  list(study = "Toutain 1984 (8 AM)", label = "IV DEX 0.05 mg/kg", clock = 8, rm = 47.89, ra = 15.23, rmax = 44.76,
       doses = data.frame(cmt = "a_blood", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 556.67), end = 96),
  list(study = "Toutain 1984 (8 AM)", label = "IV ISO 0.05 mg/kg", clock = 8, rm = 47.89, ra = 15.23, rmax = 44.76,
       doses = data.frame(cmt = "blood_iso", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 556.67 * dex_to_iso), end = 96),
  list(study = "Toutain 1984 (8 AM)", label = "IM DEX 0.05 mg/kg", clock = 8, rm = 47.89, ra = 15.23, rmax = 44.76,
       doses = data.frame(cmt = "depot_im", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 556.67), end = 96),
  list(study = "Ekstrand 2015 (9 AM)", label = "IM ISO 0.024 mg/kg", clock = 9, rm = 93.42, ra = 15.23, rmax = 0,
       doses = data.frame(cmt = "depot_im_iso", amt = 0.0239 * 1000 * 474.17 * dex_to_iso), end = 720),
  list(study = "Soma 2005 (7 AM)", label = "IV DEX 0.05 mg/kg", clock = 7, rm = 47.89, ra = 15.23, rmax = 0,
       doses = data.frame(cmt = "a_blood", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 514.5), end = 240),
  list(study = "Soma 2013 (8 AM)", label = "IV PHO 0.05 mg/kg", clock = 8, rm = 47.89, ra = 15.23, rmax = 68.09,
       doses = data.frame(cmt = "blood_pho", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 523.5 * dex_to_pho), end = 120),
  list(study = "Soma 2013 (8 AM)", label = "IA PHO 0.05 mg/kg", clock = 8, rm = 47.89, ra = 15.23, rmax = 68.09,
       doses = data.frame(cmt = "joint_pho", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 523.5 * dex_to_pho), end = 120),
  list(study = "Grady 2010 (8 AM)", label = "IV DEX 0.05 mg/kg", clock = 8, rm = 93.42, ra = 18.62, rmax = 38.73,
       doses = data.frame(cmt = "a_blood", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 507.5), end = 96),
  list(study = "Grady 2010 (8 AM)", label = "PO solution 0.05 mg/kg", clock = 8, rm = 93.42, ra = 18.62, rmax = 38.73,
       doses = data.frame(cmt = "depot_oral_liquid", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 507.5), end = 96),
  list(study = "Grady 2010 (8 AM)", label = "PO powder 0.05 mg/kg", clock = 8, rm = 93.42, ra = 18.62, rmax = 38.73,
       doses = data.frame(cmt = "depot_oral_solid", amt = 0.05 * 1000 * 507.5), end = 96)
)
# Ekstrand 2016, 10 AM: DEX_PHO bolus + 3-h infusion, 507.92 kg
for (b in infusion_levels) {
  cort_studies[[length(cort_studies) + 1]] <- list(
    study = "Ekstrand 2016 (10 AM)",
    label = sprintf("IV PHO %g ug/kg + infusion", b),
    clock = 10, rm = 47.89, ra = 18.62, rmax = 0,
    doses = data.frame(
      cmt = "blood_pho",
      amt = c(b, 0.233 * b * 3) * 507.92 * dex_to_pho,
      rate = c(0, 0.233 * b * 507.92 * dex_to_pho)
    ),
    end = 96
  )
}

fig7 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(cort_studies, function(s) {
  doses <- s$doses
  doses$time <- s$clock
  pars <- c(
    lrbase_cortisol = log(s$rm),
    lamp_cortisol = log(s$ra),
    # the stress surge is switched off for studies without one
    lrmax_stress = if (s$rmax > 0) log(s$rmax) else -Inf
  )
  obs <- s$clock + sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.02), seq(2, s$end, by = 0.5))))
  out <- simulate_one(doses, obs, params = pars, label = s$label)
  out$study <- s$study
  out$time_after_dose <- out$time - s$clock
  out
}))

ggplot(fig7, aes(time_after_dose, cortisol, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~study, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Plasma cortisol (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 7 of Yu 2026 (typical-value predictions)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

```{r fig7-check}
toutain_iv <- dplyr::filter(fig7, study == "Toutain 1984 (8 AM)", label == "IV DEX 0.05 mg/kg")
# Results: DEX reduced cortisol to almost zero (about 1 ng/mL) after
# 0.05 mg/kg; Figure 7 shows the nadir at about 12 h after the 8 AM dose.
nadir <- min(toutain_iv$cortisol)
t_nadir <- toutain_iv$time_after_dose[which.min(toutain_iv$cortisol)]
# Stress surge: cortisol rises by about Rmax,stress within 20 min (Results).
surge <- max(toutain_iv$cortisol[toutain_iv$time_after_dose <= 0.34]) - toutain_iv$cortisol[1]
# Recovery over 3-4 rhythmic cycles: by 72-96 h after the dose cortisol is
# back within 15% of its baseline.
late <- dplyr::filter(toutain_iv, time_after_dose >= 84)
bl_late <- 47.89 + 15.23 * cos(2 * pi / 24 * (late$time - 8.94))
stopifnot(
  nadir < 3,
  t_nadir > 6, t_nadir < 18,
  surge > 20, surge < 44.76,
  max(abs(late$cortisol / bl_late - 1)) < 0.15
)
c(nadir_ng_mL = nadir, nadir_time_h = t_nadir, surge_ng_mL = surge)
```

**Emax and EC50.** Table III prints Emax = 1.187 and EC50 = 0.799 ng/mL. In
the authors' ADAPT glucose code the parameter labels are `Psym(2) = 'EC50'`
and `Psym(3) = 'Emax'`, but the differential equations read `Emax = P(2)` and
`EC50 = P(3)`, so the fitted model used Emax = 0.799 and EC50 = 1.187 ng/mL
and the table reports them under each other's names. The packaged model uses
the code's assignment. The table below re-solves Figure 9 with the
Table III labels instead: every peak and the daily-IM plateau then sit well
above the fitted curves of Figure 9 and the quoted ~8.5 mM.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Authors' code followed for the blood equation.** The printed Eq. 8 writes
  the blood outflow as `Qco * Cp * Rb` and the liver inflow as
  `Ql * Cp * Rb`. The ADAPT code integrates `Cp` with the blood equation
  divided by `Vb * Rb` and applies every flow term to `Cp` without `Rb`. The
  packaged model follows the code: it is what was fitted, and it reproduces
  the paper's hepatic clearance (338 mL/h/kg), extraction ratio (28%) and total
  clearance (344 mL/h/kg), which the printed form would not. The liver
  equation follows the code in the same way (the unbound fraction `fut`
  multiplies both the hepatic outflow and the intrinsic clearance).
* **Physiological constants** are the unrounded ADAPT-code values (e.g.
  `Rb = 0.6945` against "0.69" in the text; volumes and flows against the
  rounded Table S1). Clearances are the Table II per-kg values times the
  550-kg body weight of Table S1.
* **Final estimates from Table II, not from the PD code.** The cortisol and
  glucose ADAPT files hard-code the PK parameters, and three of them differ
  from Table II: `F1 = 0.6622` (Table II `FGI` for liquids 68.2%), `Kap1 =
  4.126` and `Fp1 = 0.5642` (Table II healthy-joint `ka,IA` 2.61 1/h and `FIA`
  83.0%). Table II is used throughout. The Results text quotes slightly
  different IA values again (2.64 1/h and 82.5% healthy; 5.16 1/h inflamed,
  Table II 5.13); Table II is used.
* **Inflamed-joint input.** Eq. 7 describes the synovial-fluid DEX amount as a
  tri-exponential function of time starting at the full DEX-equivalent dose.
  It is carried as three first-order pools dosed simultaneously with the same
  prodrug amount, each with a bioavailability equal to its intercept times the
  DEX/PHO molecular-weight ratio; this is the same function and also
  superposes over repeated doses. The prodrug conversion constant `kf,IA` is
  not part of Eq. 7 and applies only to the healthy-joint route (as in the
  ADAPT code).
* **IM DEX alcohol bioavailability** is not in Table II. The ADAPT cortisol and
  glucose code fixes it at 1 (`Fml = 1`), consistent with the Results ("negligible
  absorption loss"), and the packaged model does the same.
* **Cortisol written in deviation form.** Eq. 16 is integrated as the
  deviation of cortisol from its circadian baseline: substituting Eq. 15 into
  Eq. 16 gives `d(cortisol_dev)/dt = stress - kin(t) * I(Cp) - kout *
  cortisol_dev` with `cortisol_dev(0) = 0`, and `cortisol = baseline(t) +
  cortisol_dev` is identical to Eq. 16 started on its baseline. This keeps the
  initial condition correct whatever the first record time.
* **Clock time.** The ADAPT code shifts the acrophase per study by the study
  start time (`tp = 0.94` h for 8 AM, 23.94 h for 9 AM, 22.94 h for 10 AM,
  1.94 h for 7 AM). The packaged model uses clock time as model time with a
  single acrophase of 8.94 h (8:56 AM; Table III), which is the same thing.
* **Stress surge.** The ADAPT code switches the surge on for `t < tau` with
  every study starting at its first dose. The packaged model uses time after
  the most recent dose (`tad()`), so the surge follows every dose, matching the
  Methods ("operates for the duration of tau after drug dosing"). The packaged
  default `Rmax,stress` is the paper's mean of the three study estimates
  (50.53 ng/mL), used by the paper for the Figure 8 prediction; set
  `lrmax_stress = -Inf` to remove the surge.
* **Per-study cortisol baselines.** Table III assigns `Ra = 15.23` to Grady
  2010 and Ekstrand 2015 and `Rm = 47.89` to Ekstrand 2015. The ADAPT
  cortisol code, and the baselines drawn in Figure 7, use `Rm = 93.42` for both
  Ekstrand 2015 and Grady 2010, and an amplitude of 18.62 ng/mL (not in Table
  III) for Grady 2010 and Ekstrand 2016. The Figure 7 replication uses the code
  values; the packaged defaults (Ekstrand 2019, 62.25 / 22.01 ng/mL) are
  unaffected.
* **Hill coefficients.** The ADAPT cortisol and glucose code carries a Hill
  exponent (`Gama`) that appears in neither Eq. 16 nor Eq. 17 nor Table III;
  the packaged model follows the equations (exponent 1).
* **Glucose Emax and EC50 exchanged relative to Table III.** The ADAPT glucose
  code labels `P(2)` as EC50 and `P(3)` as Emax but uses `P(2)` as Emax and
  `P(3)` as EC50 in its equations, so Table III (and the Results text, which
  follows it) prints the two estimates under each other's names. The packaged
  model uses Emax = 0.799 and EC50 = 1.187 ng/mL, which reproduces the fitted
  curves of Figure 9 and the quoted ~8.5 mM plateau; the Table III labels do
  not (Figure 9 section above). Consequently the Results' theoretical maximum
  of 11.24 mM and the comparison of EC50 with the IC50 for cortisol rest on the
  printed labels; with the fitted assignment the maximum is E0 x 1.799
  (9.25 mM at E0 = 5.14) and the EC50 is 1.19 ng/mL.
* **Glucose baseline.** Table III gives only the range of the study baselines
  (4.65-5.47 mM). The default 5.14 mM is the baseline implied by the Results
  statement that the maximal glucose "could theoretically reach 11.24 mM"
  (11.24 / (1 + 1.187), the authors' arithmetic); it also reproduces the
  quoted production rate of ~0.25 mM/h. Set `lrbase_glucose` to a study's own
  baseline when known.
* **Residual error.** The ADAPT variance model (Eq. 18) is a combined
  additive-plus-proportional standard deviation per output group, but the
  variance-parameter estimates are not reported. They are packaged as
  `fixed(0)`, so the model simulates typical-value profiles only.
* **No variability.** The data are study means, so the model has no
  between-animal or between-study random effects.
* **Doses in the figure replications** use each study's mean body weight as
  recorded in the ADAPT code comments; for the Mizen 2017 daily IM regimen
  (weight not reported) 550 kg is used. Small differences between the
  replicated curves and the published figures are expected where the paper's
  weights or dose rounding differ.
